messages:
oliver_chen: FYI spotted a perf regression on multi-GPU pipeline runs after the kernel-selection change in commit abc123. p95 tokens up ~18% on long-seq. Attached nsys + perfetto traces: https://internal-traces/redwood/1769876543 (nsys) and https://perfetto/redwood/trace/1769876543
perf-bot: regression-checker: p95_latency increased by 18% for model-x on 8xA100, change set: runtime/kernel-selection v2
priya.d: Can you paste the nvprof/nsys timeline snippet? curious if all-reduce timings shifted or if kernel launch serialization increased
oliver_chen: snippet from nsys (filtered):
```
GPU 0  GPU1  GPU2  GPU3  | NCCL allReduce  12ms | kernel conv_fwd 3ms | kernel attn 9ms
... timeline shows repeated stalls where NCCL wait overlaps with small kernel launches
```
marco_s: that smells like increased kernel breakup -> more frequent MPI/NCCL calls. Our batching heuristic may be sending smaller micro-batches after the kernel selector switched to fused-but-sparsed kernels
priya.d: Another angle: KV cache behavior? if KV cache misses are causing extra decode kernels interleaved with communication, that could break NCCL pipelining
oliver_chen: ran a perfetto capture with nvtx ranges, see region names: `batching.apply`, `kv.lookup`, `kv.insert`, `comm.allreduce`. Perfetto flame shows `kv.lookup` inserting ~700us gaps before allReduce across ranks
marco_s: do we have NCCL traces? want to check op timestamps across ranks for overlap. Can you dump nccl trace with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and nsys --trace=nvtx,nvtxrange,nccl?
oliver_chen: uploaded nccl log excerpt:
```
[Rank 0] AllReduce start 1623456789.123 end 1623456789.137
[Rank 1] AllReduce start 1623456789.124 end 1623456789.138
[Rank 2] AllReduce start 1623456789.130 end 1623456789.144
```
notice rank skew ~6-7us then tail extends because rank2 blocks on a small kernel
runtime-oncall: quick repro: run with env VARS: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=tree NCCL_STREAMS=2 and compare to NCCL_ALGO=ring. ring shows slightly better overlap in our cluster for these patterns
priya.d: try bumping batching window to accumulate 2 more requests (simulate larger micro-batch) and re-run nsys; if p95 drops then heuristic is too aggressive on early release
marco_s: also propose a hotfix: in kernel selector, prefer kernels with slightly higher single-thread latency but fewer launches for short sequences (tune threshold). I can prototype today
oliver_chen: running quick experiments now: 1) increase batch window from 5->7ms 2) force old kernel selector 3) set NCCL_ALGO=ring. Will post traces in ~20m
perf-bot: jira#INF-892 created: multigpu-allreduce-pipeline-skew. Attached: nsys trace, nccl logs, perfetto html
priya.d: thanks. If the quick experiments validate, let's schedule a canary rollout to dedicated cluster before prod
oliver_chen: results: forcing old selector drops p95 by ~12%, increasing batch window drops another ~6%. NCCL_ALGO=ring mostly helps tail on this config. Looks like combination fix: revert hasty selector heuristic + tweak batching default
marco_s: I'll open PR with fallback to the previous kernel-selection threshold and add telemetry counters for `kv.lookup` latency and `comm.skew_ms` to help triage automatically
oliver_chen: cool. I'll attach the final nsys profile and the perfetto link to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
